html:
Spanish conquistador who brought down the Aztec Empire between 1519 and 1521. Born in Medellín, in western Spain, he went to Hispaniola in 1504 and helped conquer Cuba.

In 1519 he sailed for Mexico against the orders of Cuba's governor, with about 500 men. An Indigenous woman, Malintzin, became his interpreter and adviser. He won thousands of allies among peoples who resented Aztec rule, above all the Tlaxcalans.

  • November 1519: entered Tenochtitlan and took Moctezuma II hostage.
  • June 1520: driven out of the city with heavy losses.
  • 1520: smallpox killed many in the city.
  • August 1521: after a long siege, the city fell.

Cortés governed what became New Spain for a few years, but the crown soon sent officials to replace him. He led more expeditions, to Honduras and Baja California, then went back to Spain, where he died in 1547.
sum: Spanish conquistador who brought down the Aztec Empire between 1519 and 1521. Born in Medellín, in western Spain, he went to Hispaniola in 1504 and helped conquer Cuba.
